question: What is 'hungry bone syndrome', which can happen right after a parathyroidectomy?

question: How does using the nursing process in critical care differ from a normal ward?

options.A: 75 to 90 degrees
options.B: 5 to 10 degrees

options.D: 15 to 30 degrees

explanation: An angle of 15 to 30 degrees is the sweet spot! It lets you slide right through the skin and gently catch the superficial vein without poking through the back wall. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h3)

question: Why is it so important to set rehabilitation goals together with the patient?

options.A: Patients usually know more about pharmacology than doctors do
options.B: Hospital policies legally forbid nurses from writing goals alone
options.C: Goals matter more and motivate the patient when they reflect personal values
options.D: Collaborative goals take less time to write out in charts

explanation: When patients help choose their goals, they feel heard and stay much more motivated to work hard during therapy! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T2#GNS123_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do for active bleeding from an arm wound?

options.A: Elevate the arm and wait
options.B: Wash the open wound thoroughly with cold water
options.C: Apply firm, direct pressure with a clean dressing
options.D: Tie a tight tourniquet above the elbow

question: What is the medical term for the warning signs that happen just before a person faints?

options.A: Aura
options.B: Prodrome
options.C: Shock
options.D: Seizure

explanation: The prodrome refers to the early symptoms like sweating and dizziness that signal a faint is coming. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h4)

question: What is the most important part of sexual consent?

options.A: Long-term plans for marriage and children
options.B: Financial stability of both individuals involved
options.C: Voluntary and clear agreement from all parties
options.D: Approval from parents or legal guardians

explanation: Spot on! True consent must always be given freely, clearly, and without any pressure or force. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard immediate action when caring for a patient in shock?

options.A: Providing high-flow oxygen
options.B: Administering a large oral meal
options.C: Establishing large-bore IV access
options.D: Applying warm blankets

explanation: Patients in shock have poor gut perfusion and are at high risk for aspiration, so oral food and fluids are strictly withheld. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which cells in the pancreas release insulin to lower your blood sugar after a meal?

options.A: Alpha cells
options.B: Delta cells
options.C: Acinar cells
options.D: Beta cells

explanation: Pancreatic beta cells are your body's sugar sweepers—they release insulin to help cells soak up glucose after you eat. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the golden rule for managing different kinds of waste safely?

options.A: Dumping liquid waste near water wells
options.B: Segregation at the source
options.C: Burning everything in an open field
options.D: Mixing all refuse together to save time

explanation: You got it! Sorting waste right where you drop it keeps dangerous things like used needles away from regular household trash. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the standard dose of PPD administered during a Mantoux test?

options.B: 0.1 mL containing 5 tuberculin units
options.C: 0.5 mL containing 10 tuberculin units
options.D: 2.0 mL containing 100 tuberculin units

question: In the ABCDE primary survey, what does the letter 'D' stand for?

options.A: Disability
options.B: Diagnosis
options.C: Drainage
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: D is for Disability! It is just a quick check of the patient's neurological status and brain function. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h2)

question: What safety step is required if a patient experiencing cardiac arrest is lying in a puddle of water?

options.A: Turn off all nearby electrical appliances in the room
options.B: Double the number of chest compressions you deliver
options.C: Move the patient to a dry area and dry the chest
options.D: Place rubber mats under your own shoes while working

explanation: Water conducts electricity. Moving the patient to dry ground and wiping their chest ensures the shock goes through the heart, not out into the water. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a cerebral angiography test?

options.A: To drain extra fluid from the brain ventricles
options.B: To measure electrical activity in the brain
options.C: To check the bone thickness at the skull base
options.D: To visualize blood vessels and spot aneurysms or blockages

explanation: Angiography uses dye to map out the brain's blood vessels, helping find narrow spots or weak bulging areas. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T8#GNS222_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why should nurses rotate injection sites for patients who need frequent medications?

options.A: It ensures the medication reaches the bloodstream much faster
options.B: It stops bacteria from multiplying on the surface of the skin
options.C: It gives previous tissue time to heal instead of forming hard scar tissue
options.D: It prevents the needle from becoming dull during the procedure

explanation: Sticking the exact same spot over and over causes fibrous scar knots, which hurt the patient and make drug absorption difficult. Rotating sites keeps tissue healthy! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: How do tiny villi and microvilli help the small intestine do its job better?

options.A: By producing strong acid to break down tough plant fibers
options.B: By pushing waste products quickly toward the large bowel
options.C: By greatly increasing the surface area available for absorption
options.D: By storing excess water during times of dehydration

explanation: Brilliant! These tiny finger-like folds give the small intestine a massive surface area so it can soak up as many nutrients as possible. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h4)

question: Carbon monoxide causes chemical asphyxiation mainly because it:

options.A: Blocks the physical entry of air into the nose
options.B: Causes an immediate severe allergic reaction
options.C: Stops body cells from using oxygen properly
options.D: Crushes the chest wall from the outside

question: Why should you teach deep breathing and coughing exercises along with giving an expectorant?

options.A: To slow down the heart rate during coughing fits
options.B: To stretch the chest wall muscles and prevent cramping
options.C: To help physically expel the mucus that the medication has loosened
options.D: To replace the need for drinking water during the daytime

explanation: Spot on! The medicine loosens the phlegm up, but good breathing and controlled coughing give the patient the muscle power to get it all out. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why is drug synergism especially helpful when fighting bacterial infections?

options.A: It helps prevent or delay the development of drug resistance
options.B: It guarantees that side effects will never occur
options.C: It eliminates the need for any patient fluid intake
options.D: It turns antibiotics into vitamins that nourish body tissues

explanation: When we attack germs on multiple fronts at once, it makes it super difficult for them to mutate and build resistance to our drugs. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T6#GNS125_U5_T6_h5)

question: Why do low-income communities often experience higher rates of endemic waterborne diseases?

options.A: Overcrowded schools running multiple shifts daily
options.B: Lack of proper sanitation infrastructure and safe drinking water
options.C: Higher consumption of locally brewed herbal beverages
options.D: Greater resistance of local bacteria to standard antibiotics

explanation: Without clean water systems and proper sewage disposal, water sources easily become contaminated with disease-causing microorganisms. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h4)

question: Why can minor physiological disturbances quickly become dangerous in critically ill patients?

options.A: Hospital rooms are usually too cold for recovery.
options.B: Their organ systems are already operating near total failure.
options.C: Laboratory tests are rarely accurate in acute settings.
options.D: Intravenous lines frequently disconnect by themselves.

explanation: When organs have little reserve left, even a small stressor can tip the patient over the edge into complete system failure. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h1)

question: If a client reports mild, normal side effects from her contraceptive, which action is NOT helpful?

options.A: Dismissing their concerns as imaginary
options.B: Providing reassurance and timeline expectations
options.C: Validating their physical experience
options.D: Explaining simple ways to manage the symptoms

explanation: Never brush off a client's feelings! Listening, validating, and supporting them builds trust and helps them stick to their care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: A patient stops shaking after a seizure, falls into a deep, snoring sleep, and feels confused when woken up. What nursing term describes this phase?

options.A: Aura phase
options.B: Tonic phase
options.C: Postictal phase
options.D: Clonic phase

question: Which of these is NOT a sign or effect of Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)?

options.A: Presence of multiple small ovarian cysts
options.B: Irregular or absent ovulation
options.C: Interference with normal follicular development
options.D: Continuous production of excess mature ova

explanation: PCOS actually makes normal ovulation harder, rather than flooding the body with extra healthy, mature eggs. You're mastering this! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T9#GNS121_U5_T9_h7)

question: What should a nurse do if a medical doctor prescribes an obviously dangerous dose of a controlled drug?

options.A: Question the order and clarify with the prescriber before giving it
options.B: Throw the medication away without telling anyone
options.C: Ask another patient to take the extra dose instead
options.D: Administer the medication anyway since the doctor signed it

explanation: Nurses are legally responsible for the medications they administer and must question unsafe orders. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h5)

question: Where do you deposit medication when giving a subcutaneous injection?

options.A: Inside the main muscle belly
options.B: Into the layer of fat beneath the skin
options.C: Directly into the bone marrow
options.D: Inside a major circulating vein

explanation: Great job! Subcutaneous simply means 'under the skin,' targeting that nice fatty layer resting right between the dermis and the muscle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h1)

question: A patient recovering from defibulation surgery is in the ward. What is a key nursing priority?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to keep the surgical site dry
options.B: Applying tight pressure dressings to keep edges closed
options.C: Providing meticulous wound care to prevent new adhesion formation
options.D: Encouraging immediate heavy exercise to build strength

explanation: That's correct! Freshly separated wound edges can easily stick back together, making careful hygiene and separation techniques key nursing duties. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h4)

question: What main factor helps doctors decide whether to use surgery or radiation for cervical cancer?

options.C: The availability of blood donors in the local hospital ward
options.D: The exact blood type of the individual diagnosed

explanation: Exactly! Early stages are often fixed with surgery, while more advanced stages need a mix of radiation and drugs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h6)

question: How often should an antenatal clinic see a pregnant woman with sickle cell disease during her first two trimesters?

options.A: Every two weeks
options.B: Only in emergencies
options.C: Twice a week
options.D: Once every month

explanation: Spot on. High-risk pregnancies need close monitoring right from the start—usually every two weeks to catch any problems early. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h3)

question: You just finished soaking and washing your patient's hands. What is the most important thing to do before picking up the clippers?

options.A: Applying thick scented lotion to the skin
options.B: Pushing the cuticles back with force
options.C: Drying the hands and fingers thoroughly
options.D: Massaging the palms to improve circulation

question: Where do the coronary arteries, which feed the heart muscle itself, take their origin?

options.A: The pulmonary veins
options.B: The base of the aorta
options.C: The right atrium
options.D: The superior vena cava

question: What is the main job of the mucociliary escalator in our airways?

options.A: Exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide in the tiny air sacs
options.B: Making surfactant to keep the lungs from collapsing
options.C: Filtering big dust bits right inside the nose
options.D: Sweeping trapped dirt and mucus upward toward the throat

explanation: Think of the mucociliary escalator like a tiny conveyor belt in your respiratory tract. It uses beating hair-like cilia and mucus to push dust and germs up to your throat so you can swallow or cough them out cleanly! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T13#GNS213_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which topical preparation is best suited for treating thick, dry, and scaly skin lesions?

options.A: A watery lotion
options.B: An oil-based ointment
options.C: A fast-drying powder
options.D: An alcohol-based liquid

question: As shock becomes more severe and progressive, what acid-base imbalance usually develops?

options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

question: Why do patients with chronic renal failure frequently look very pale and complain of severe tiredness?

options.D: High potassium levels destroy red blood cells in the bloodstream.

question: What is the single most common cause of chronic renal failure here in Nigeria?

question: What test is mainly used to check for a broken bone after a bad joint injury?

question: What makes an expected outcome (goal) well-written?

question: Which of these is NOT a correct nursing action when caring for a patient with an active adrenal disorder?

question: What is a common patient misconception regarding injections that nurses should actively address?

question: What is a common physical risk of giving artificial IV hydration to a terminal patient?

question: Which bony area is at the highest risk for pressure sores when a patient lies flat on their back?

options.B: Forehead
options.C: Kneecap
options.D: Sacrum

question: A patient with Parkinson's disease cannot swallow large pills, and their prescribed capsule is extended-release. What is the safest nursing action?

question: Your clinic gets a donation of mosquito nets and supplements. Who should you give priority to?

question: How does chronic psychological stress directly impact the cardiovascular system?

options.D: By keeping stress hormones elevated, which raises blood pressure and inflammation

explanation: Prolonged stress floods the body with adrenaline and cortisol, raising blood pressure, increasing heart rate, and promoting inflammatory changes in blood vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h7)

question: What is a must-do nursing action before giving any new medication to a patient?

options.B: Obtaining written consent from the family
options.C: Checking for known drug allergies
options.D: Drawing a baseline complete blood count

question: Why do nurses check and feel (palpate) the neck during a physical assessment of the mouth?

question: What is the main risk of breastfeeding when a mother is living with HIV?

options.D: Permanent loss of breast milk production

question: Why do patients on blood thinners still rely on their body's natural healing to clear old clots?

options.C: Anticoagulants lack the ability to break down established fibrin
options.D: Anticoagulants only slow down the heart rate

question: Which of these tools do you need on your clean workspace when mixing a topical dilution?

options.B: A clean mixing tile and spatula
options.C: A sterile surgical scalpel
options.D: A glass measuring cup for oral liquids

question: Why is Visual Inspection with Acetic Acid (VIA) so helpful in primary healthcare clinics across Nigeria?

question: Why are antiplatelet drugs like aspirin given to patients with peripheral artery disease?

options.D: To keep platelets from sticking together and forming new clots

question: What is a recommended safety item for a patient diagnosed with a chronic seizure disorder to wear at all times?

options.C: A hard plastic safety helmet
options.D: A bright yellow reflective vest

question: Why must nurses balance medical treatments with a resident's personal wishes?

options.C: To respect resident dignity while still achieving safe, effective outcomes.
options.D: To completely bypass hospital discharge regulations.

question: Which sign requires your immediate, urgent attention after a patient receives an intrapleural medication?

options.C: Sudden respiratory distress and falling oxygen saturation

question: Why do nurses do a baseline neurologic assessment when a patient is first admitted?

question: A patient was just extubated 20 minutes ago and now has a high-pitched whistling sound when breathing in. What is the most likely cause?

question: What is the best way to respond when a grieving family member is crying silently at the bedside?

options.C: Sit quietly nearby and offer a supportive physical presence
options.D: Tell a cheerful story to distract them from their sadness

question: What is the primary role of the nurse on a multidisciplinary endocrine care team?

options.C: Managing hospital financial budgets
options.D: Prescribing all specialized medications independently

question: What does it mean when a cancer cell is called 'poorly differentiated'?

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the classic 5 Ps assessed during neurovascular checks?

question: Why do we encourage patients to get up and walk early after pelvic or reproductive surgery?

question: Why do we recommend putting petroleum jelly on a healing biopsy site instead of letting a hard crust form?

question: What major hazard happens when sharps disposal boxes are allowed to become overfilled?

question: What is a major long-term risk of persistent, chronic inflammation in the body?

question: Why is it helpful for the body to use direct nerve control during sudden danger?

question: As a nurse, you discover that a 13-year-old patient is scheduled to be married next week. What is your immediate professional duty?

question: What is the primary purpose of therapeutic communication in palliative care?

question: What is the main job of the sticky electrode pads on an AED?

question: Why is patient education a powerful nursing tool against under-prescription?

question: A patient just returned to the ward after a cerebral angiogram through the groin. What is a key nursing duty?

question: Which nursing finding in a patient with belly pain is most urgent and needs an immediate call to the doctor?

options.A: A single episode of greenish-yellow vomit with food in it
options.B: A rigid, board-like belly with severe tenderness when you let go (rebound tenderness)
options.C: Mild nausea when the patient tries to sip water
options.D: Slowing bowel sounds heard four hours after surgery

explanation: A board-like rigid belly is a red flag for peritonitis (inflammation of the abdominal lining), which can rapidly progress to life-threatening sepsis if ignored. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h7)

question: Why do we need to check the expiration dates on AED electrode pads?

options.A: Old pads contain chemicals that become toxic when exposed to air.
options.B: The computer software will refuse to turn on if attached to expired pads.
options.C: Expired pads will automatically trigger a loud alarm that disrupts hospital wards.
options.D: The conductive gel on the pads can dry out over time, preventing proper shock delivery.

explanation: Over time, the sticky gel on the pads dries out. If the gel goes bad, the electricity won't pass through properly during a rescue. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h6)

question: Why do we have to be extra careful when disposing of cytotoxic (chemotherapy) drugs?

options.A: Expired tablets turn into sweet-tasting candy that attracts children
options.B: These drugs instantly catch fire when exposed to ordinary air
options.C: Cytotoxic drugs are designed to destroy cells and can damage healthy tissue and genetic material
options.D: Chemotherapy drugs make the local soil extremely fertile for crops

explanation: Spot on! These medications are specially made to kill fast-growing cells, meaning they can harm healthy human tissue and our environment if carelessly thrown out. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why do nurses carry a major responsibility in maintaining injection safety?

options.A: They purchase all medical equipment used in the healthcare facility
options.B: They are responsible for manufacturing sterile needles in the hospital
options.C: They dictate the national health policies regarding infectious waste
options.D: They are the primary healthcare workers who administer injections to patients

explanation: Nurses are directly responsible for preparing and administering injections, placing them at the center of safety protocol execution. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: You walk into a patient's room and see a big loop of chest tube tubing resting on the floor. What should you do first?

options.A: Clamp the chest tube immediately and page the physician for urgent removal
options.B: Lift the drainage canister up and place it on the patient's bed
options.C: Adjust the tubing so it coils loosely on the bed and drains freely without kinks
options.D: Disconnect the tubing joints to empty the pooled fluid onto the floor

explanation: Spot on! Dependent loops trap fluid and block drainage. Arranging the tubing neatly on the bed lets everything flow smoothly again. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T18#GNS221_U2_T18_h4)

question: What is a top nursing priority right after a reproductive surgery like a hysterectomy?

options.A: Restricting all fluid intake for the first 48 hours
options.B: Monitoring vital signs closely for signs of hemorrhage or infection
options.C: Preventing the patient from moving or walking for a week
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately to free up hospital beds

explanation: Spot on! Right after surgery, keeping a close eye on vitals helps you catch early warning signs of bleeding or infection. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T14#GNS311_U1_T14_h5)

question: How do sperm travel upward through the long vas deferens during ejaculation?

options.A: By beating their flagella very rapidly
options.B: By suction created by the prostate gland
options.C: By smooth muscle peristaltic contractions
options.D: By gravity pulling them down into the urethra

explanation: Just like food moves down your gut, the walls of the vas deferens use wave-like muscle squeezes (peristalsis) to push sperm smoothly along their journey. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h3)

question: What can happen if ear drops are administered while they are too cold?

options.A: Infection of the outer ear
options.B: Dizziness and vertigo
options.C: Immediate hearing loss
options.D: Swelling of the earlobe

explanation: Cold liquid near the eardrum stimulates the inner ear balance centers, triggering sudden dizziness and nausea. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the main goal of disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) in treating disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: To immediately repair severed nerve axons overnight
options.B: To reduce relapse frequency and slow long-term disability
options.C: To completely cure the underlying autoimmune response
options.D: To lower elevated blood pressure caused by stress

explanation: While they don't offer an instant cure, DMTs help calm the immune system over time, preventing future attacks and keeping the patient independent longer. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T3#GNS222_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is a physical safety feature (engineering control) built to stop sharps injuries?

options.A: Retractable scalpel blades
options.B: Doing yearly staff performance reviews
options.C: Giving verbal warnings across the theatre table
options.D: Wearing plain cotton scrub suits

explanation: Engineering controls are physical tools or devices built right into equipment—like a retractable blade—to keep us safe from accidental cuts. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T12#GNS123_U5_T12_h7)

question: When is the best time to give antiemetic (anti-nausea) medication to a palliative patient who struggles with nausea at meal times?

options.A: Right before bedtime
options.B: Only when the patient falls asleep
options.C: Right after finishing a large plate
options.D: Before meals

explanation: Well reasoned! Giving the anti-nausea medicine ahead of time stops nausea before it starts, helping the patient actually enjoy a few bites of food. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T17#GNS321_U4_T17_h3)

question: Why is discussing the realities of life support important during advance care planning?

options.A: It reduces the amount of paperwork nurses must file in the chart
options.B: It prevents family members from ever disagreeing with the doctor
options.C: It helps patients give truly informed consent for what they want or reject
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will live longer in the hospital

explanation: Patients need to know what procedures like CPR or ventilation actually involve so their choices are genuinely informed. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: When is the best time to check back on a patient after giving them oral pain medication?

options.A: Before the next scheduled meal
options.B: Within 30 to 60 minutes
options.C: Immediately upon injection
options.D: After exactly 24 hours

explanation: Oral meds usually take 30 to 60 minutes to kick in. That's your window to return and see if the drug is doing its job! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h6)

question: Which of these is a common way gender bias shows up in clinical care?

options.A: Children being denied vaccines based on their biological sex
options.B: Men receiving lower doses of routine prescription antibiotics
options.C: Women's physical pain symptoms being dismissed as emotional
options.D: Healthcare workers ignoring male patients with broken bones

explanation: Studies show healthcare providers are sometimes too quick to brush off women's physical pain, wrongly chalking it up to emotional stress instead of looking for a medical cause. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T5#GNS312_U4_T5_h3)
